title: Prove exact twenty-two-term tariffs for Boolean fanout triples
body:
The Boolean-product demand `(110,101,011)` now has an exact **22-term tariff for every strictly positive destination-row price vector**, with matching constructions and an all-word lower bound. This resolves Open next question 1 of #5259. Its one-insertion cost-16 example was previously only an upper bound; it is now proved optimal at those prices.

With insertion price `mu_i` and ADD price `c_i` for the receiving row, write `{i,j,k}={0,1,2}`:

```text
D   = mu_0 + mu_1 + mu_2
T_i = 2mu_i + 2c_j + 2c_k
B_k = mu_i + mu_j + 2c_k + min(mu_i,mu_j,2c_i,2c_j,2c_k)
U_i = mu_i + 2(c_0+c_1+c_2)
OPT = min(D,T_0,T_1,T_2,B_0,B_1,B_2,U_0,U_1,U_2).
```

The new branch proves that a single insertion at row i requires at least two ADDs into **every** row: its coefficient must generate the full demand ideal, while no individual target does, and restoration rules out exactly one incoming ADD. A three-ADD suffix and its inverse attain those six additions. The nineteen multi-insertion vectors from #5259 remain necessary; the three U vectors complete the Pareto frontier. Explicit positive prices expose every vector uniquely.

The self-contained proof extends to every commutative unital Boolean ring, including infinite rings and proper demand ideals, provided the demands sum to zero and their principal ideals are pairwise incomparable. For uniform prices it simplifies to `min(3mu,mu+6c)`. Exactly three arbitrary dirty rows and one preserved disjoint source are allowed; coefficients and directed pairs are unrestricted, but prices depend only on receiving row and operation type.

Only five new files in `research/boolean-triple-fanout/` are changed. The original task card, changed donor-assigned scope, source attribution, mathematical proof, bounded standard-library verifier and next questions are included. No selected-frontier file is changed and no new kappa or physical supplier admission is claimed.

Validation at contribution head `c8bf34c359b3a12f112078f0072b4ecc7a942109`:

- CPython 3.12.13 normal and optimized isolated, warning-strict checks agree. Three Boolean rings cover 456 demand triples, 10,032 words, 80,256 formal forward/inverse column checks and 180,224 literal scalar checks; all 22 count vectors are strictly exposed, with eleven boundary controls.
- A separate packed-state bidirectional Dijkstra implementation allows all 63 nonzero primitives, all original dirt columns and arbitrary interleavings, without a length cutoff or formula-based pruning. Seven exact-price cases cover all six families plus rational prices; they settle 314,361 states in total and return independently replayed and charged words. This is not an enumeration of the entire affine graph.
- Three disposable optimized-mode mutations fail: undercharging U, omitting its dirt preparation and ignoring heterogeneous oracle prices.
- Both registered commands, metadata/source pins, exact committed bytes and the official export integrity check pass. Both warning-strict modes also pass from a read-only export outside Git with `PATH=/nonexistent`, identical output and all six exported files unchanged. The optional full-history preflight was not run in this shallow checkout; every declared Git provenance pin refers to the direct main parent.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/boolean-triple-fanout
```

Base: freshly fetched canonical main `ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf`, priority revision 7, unchanged at the 16:40 UTC submission refresh. Entry checks used complete snapshots of 347 open PRs and 4,548 Discussion records, then live all-state fanout PR searches and board/#1166/#5030 updates. The submission refresh read the new #5300 as well: it extends source-insertion **count** to finite associative rings and explicitly leaves total tariffs open. #5266/#5269 likewise do not resolve this price question. No competing same-tariff result or active claim appeared in the inspected records. Sparse local notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits. [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5030#discussioncomment-19149863).

Credit lee-phys #5259 for the existing nineteen vectors, words, Boolean witness and adapted verifier infrastructure; Ali Romman #5266/#5300 for the many-row insertion-count results; #5139/#5163, Nick Petalas #5208/#4916, Krzysztof Wojt #5045, Ross Richardson #3063/#3121 and the earlier fanout lineage. The pending predecessor is precisely cited and its needed arguments/code are reproduced or adapted locally; replay does not fetch or import its unmerged Git objects. Prepared by lee-phys with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent reviewers were used. Apache-2.0.

The universal statement rests on the written proof; finite checks do not provide independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance. Independently directed-edge prices, extra helpers, non-Boolean carriers and physical supplier accounting are outside this contract.

Planning and the focused replay completed successfully; the latter executes both registered normal and optimized commands. Run metadata confirms `completed`, `success` and head `c8bf34c359b3a12f112078f0072b4ecc7a942109`. No review submissions or conversation comments were present at the final check.
